correctness.rationale: The successor of each binary n-factor is an invertible feedback permutation, and unique n-factors fix the lexicographic order of BWT rows. The incoming-bit and outgoing-bit calculations prove the complete forward and reverse two-bit block identities for all n>=2. A direct count of internal and interblock changes proves both exact run formulas. At n=5 the verified bounded 2^16-mask exhaustive scan is a bijection onto all 2048 necklaces; a disjoint Euler-tour construction independently recovers the same set and exact 36-cell joint table. Direct BWT rotation sorting of each word and its reversal agrees with the symbolic formula. This is a proof plus reproducible finite exhaustive certificate, not extrapolation from a sample.

originality.rationale: The earlier order-five one-sided BWT-run histogram is already known and is not claimed as novel. Previous de Bruijn BWT work provides the complementary pair-block property, and earlier reversal BWT work gives bounds and Fibonacci-plus examples, but the inspected sources do not establish the full bit-reversal transport between forward and reversed de Bruijn necklaces. value.rationale: BWT-run count governs the space of run-based compressed indexes, and reversal sensitivity is an explicit mathematical question. De Bruijn cycles hold factor coverage perfectly fixed, isolating the impact of orientation. The general bit-reversal block transport is a reusable structural algorithm for every order, rather than an arbitrary finite slice. The exact first substantial order-five discrepancy (eight runs, eight extremizing cycles), 648 equal-run cycles, and full correlation table clarify what marginal distributions omit.
